To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the thermal and stress fields formed during LSFF process are the key factors that govern the microstructure formation of the successive layers.
the thermal and stress fields are responsible for the formation of the microstructural features and the microstructural features are responsible for the physical properties of LSFF parts.
The microstructures of successive layers of the fabricated thin wall are different due to the variation of cooling rates, which is induced by the temperature field and the stress field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of microstructures in LSFF process and the effects of the thermal and stress fields on them.
the formation of microstructure in the LSFF process and its correlation with the temperature and stress fields.
the microstructure formation in a thin wall of a laser deposited material.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LSFF process is not an isothermal solidification process, and the local microstructures are determined by the temperature and stress fields induced during the process.
the local microstructures of the deposited layers of the thin wall are determined by the temperature distribution, the cooling rate, and the stress field.
a thin wall fabricated by LSFF process can have different microstructural features at different locations, and this is a consequence of the local variations in the thermal and stress fields.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a coupled numerical and experimental approach can help to understand the complex interactions between the process parameters and the resulting microstructure formation in LSFF.
the stress field and temperature gradient induced by a moving laser in LSFF process can be used for the microstructure control and the formation of desired microstructures.
the microstructures formed in the successive layers are not only determined by the cooling rates but also the thermal stresses induced during the LSFF process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a coupled numerical-experimental approach can be employed to predict the microstructures and consequently to control the physical properties of additive manufactured parts.
a coupled thermal-mechanical simulation can be employed to predict the microstructural evolution and consequently the mechanical properties of the fabricated part.
the microstructures formed in LSFF process are not homogeneous throughout the fabricated part.
